newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore economic growth picks up in last quarter.
newsitem.headline: Singapore economic growth picks up in last quarter.

text.p: Singapore's growth picked up in the fourth quarter of 1996 after a third quarter slowdown, and there were signs of improvement in the key electronics sector, Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong said on Wednesday.
State television quoted Yeo as saying he was happy with Singapore's 6.5 percent overall economic growth in 1996, a figure announced on Tuesday by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong.

The annual figure was half a percentage point higher than the last official forecast, and was possible because of a 4.0 percent growth rate in the fourth quarter, up from 3.2 percent in the third, Yeo said.
Yeo said the key factor in the recovery was the improving electronics sector globally.
Latest figures from the United States show a surge in new orders for computer chips, a good sign that the sector was on the way to recovery. That should benefit the local electronics sector, he said.
Electronics exports are a key part of Singapore's trade, and a sag in the sector earlier in 1996 hurt the city state's overall economic performance.

The 6.5 percent 1996 growth rate announced by Prime Minister Goh on Tuesday was in line with market forecasts, although at mid-year before the electronics slump the government had forecast growth of between 7.5 and 8.5 percent.
The 1996 outcome represents a slowdown from the 8.8 percent growth rate of 1995 and the double digit growth rates of the previous two years.
